brief: Friday printed the year's lowest cash equity volume, the lowest intraday VIX at 13.8, and the second lowest average single stock vol near 30.5, but the note argues the autumn calendar of inflation and job prints, a possible Fed hike, US midterms, conferences, AI releases and earnings will lift both activity and volatility into December, with geopolitics the wildcard. The market prices a 60% chance of a 16 September hike, up from about 30% before Jackson Hole, while the GS house view stays no hike, making Tuesday's PPI and Friday's CPI the decisive datapoints. The SPX surface looks unconcerned, with the Friday straddle at 100bps. The long end is the larger risk: the 30 year yield one month average is above 5.2% for the first time since 2003, and sticky inflation, Treasury supply and term premium rebuilding can push it higher without a hike. Implied vol sits at year to date lows, six month SPX realized correlation of 11 has only two precedents in 25 years and historically ends in index vol convexity, and GS prime brokerage net and gross are back at April to May 2025 lows, which the note reads as a market not full on exposure.
